paper.title: Contextual Bandit Optimization with Pre-Trained Neural Networks

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic contextual bandit with pre-training (weak training / Assumptions 1-3)
unmapped: Reward model is a neural network w^T phi_theta(x) with realizable true weights (w*, theta*); learner is given pre-trained representation weights theta_0
Each context provides features for K actions; contexts i.i.d., action features share a common marginal D_X
Bounded weights ||w*||<=B_w, ||theta*||<=B_theta, ||phi||<=B_phi, Jacobian norm <=L_phi; noise |eta|<=B_eta i.i.d. zero mean
Misspecification of pre-trained weights measured by eps_0^2 = E[(w*^T(phi_theta0(X)-phi_theta*(X)))^2]
settings.definition_quote: An agent observes a random sequence of contexts $C_1,\ldots,C_T$, each context providing features for $K$ actions ... The agent selects an action $A_t\in[K]$ and observes the reward $r_{t,A_t}$. ... $r_{t,a}=\wstartp\pstar(X_{t,a})+\eta_{t}$

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic contextual bandit with pre-training, locally convex risk (Assumptions 1-5)
unmapped: Neural reward model w^T phi_theta(x), realizable; learner given pre-trained theta_0 and the norm bounds B_w, B_theta (projection domains)
Mean-squared risk is convex in a basin {||w-w*||_{Sigma0}^2+||theta-theta*||^2<eps_c^2} (Assumption 4)
Quality of pre-trained weights: 2 eps_0^2 d + eps_theta^2 < eps_c^2 (Assumption 5)
Bounded weights, features, Jacobian, and noise
settings.definition_quote: There exists $0<\epsilon_c<1$ such that $\risk(\w,\theta)$ is convex in the region $\conv$ around $(\wstar,\theta^*)$ ... The provided $\theta_0$ satisfies $2\epsilon_0^2d+\epsilon_\theta^2<\epsilon_c^2$

settings.name_in_paper: projected SGD on a (locally) convex risk over a ball
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Stochastic convex optimization with unbiased bounded stochastic gradients (not an interactive bandit problem)
unmapped: Domain is a ball of radius B_omega; stochastic gradients bounded by D a.s.
Learner knows D and B_omega to set the step size
settings.definition_quote: Let $\risk: \dom\to \R$ be defined over this set as $\risk(\omega)=\E_{\mathbf{z}\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[ \ell(\omega,\mathbf{z}) \right]$ ... $\omega_{t+1}:=\Pi_\mathcal{B}(\omega_t-\zeta \mathbf{v}_t)$

source.label: thm:main
source.quote:
such that, for $T_1\ge N_1$, the following statements hold simultaneously with probability not less than $1-10\delta$:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\norm{\wzero-\wstar}_{\Sigma_0}<\epsilon_\w$.
  \item For all $t=1,\ldots,T_2$, $(\w_t,\theta_t)\in \conv$.
  \item The final suboptimality gap is bounded by
    \begin{multline}
       \risk(\overline{\w}, \overline{\theta})-\risk(\wstar,\theta^*)< \frac{1}{2\zeta T_2}\left(\left(\sqrt{d(\epsilon_0^2+\epsilon_{\delta })}+\epsilon_\eta+\sqrt{\lambda} \norm{\wstar}\right)^2+\epsilon_\theta^2\right) \\
       +\frac{\zeta D_\w^2}{2\lambda} +\frac{\zeta D_\theta^2}{2}+Q_\delta,

results.notes: Excess-risk (sample complexity type) bound after the two exploration stages, probability >= 1-10 delta. ||w*|| replaced by its bound B_w.
